settings.label: Synchronization
settings.description:
None: No synchronization.
Vertical Sync: Synchronize on video sync, avoids video tearing at the price of high visual latency.
Adaptive Sync: Synchronize on video sync, except for late frames (below target FPS), also features higher visual latency.
Frame Pacing: pace the frame rendering to limit visual latency, comes with the risk of introducing more stutters if the computer is not powerful enough.

settings.label: Limit Framerate
settings.description:
-1 will limit FPS to the display refresh rate
0 will not limit the display refresh rate
Other values will limit the FPS to it (energy saving/less heat, framerate stability)

settings.label: Max. Prerendered Frames
settings.description:
Maximum number of 'frames in flight' (frames pushed to the GPU queue waiting for rendering).
Higher values may lead to higher FPS, but at higher input latency.
Recommended to be adjusted to the lowest value that allows a stable framerate.
(Not supported in OpenGL version)

settings.label: Alternative Depth Buffer

settings.label: Reflection Quality
settings.description:
Limit the quality of reflections for better performance.
'Dynamic' is recommended and will give the best results, but may harm performance.
'Static Only' has no performance cost (except for VR rendering).
Other options feature different trade-offs between quality and performance.

settings.label: Full Scene Anti Aliasing
settings.description:
Enables brute-force Up/Downsampling (similar to DSR).
This delivers very good quality but has a significant impact on performance.
200% means twice the resolution to be handled while rendering

settings.label: MSAA level

Set the amount of MSAA samples.
MSAA can help reduce geometry aliasing at the cost of performance and GPU memory.
This can improve image quality if not using supersampling
